territorial_scope.description: Amends Colorado Revised Statutes sections 6-1-1702 to 6-1-1704, state-level duties for developers and deployers of high-risk artificial intelligence systems.

evidence.quote: In Colorado Revised Statutes, 6-1-1702, amend (1),

summary.short: Colorado Senate Bill 25B-004 moves from February 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026 the start date of duties for developers and deployers of high-risk artificial intelligence systems under Colorado Revised Statutes sections 6-1-1702 to 6-1-1704, which cover algorithmic discrimination, impact assessments and AI-interaction disclosure.
summary.long: Senate Bill 25B-004 moves from February 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026 the start date of duties for developers and deployers of high-risk artificial intelligence systems in Colorado Revised Statutes sections 6-1-1702 to 6-1-1704. Developers must use reasonable care against known or reasonably foreseeable algorithmic discrimination, give deployers documentation for impact assessments, publish a website statement on their systems, and disclose such risks to the attorney general and known deployers. Deployers must use reasonable care, implement a risk management policy and program, complete impact assessments at least annually and within ninety days after an intentional and substantial modification, and report discovered algorithmic discrimination within ninety days. Deployers must also inform consumers of adverse consequential decisions, and deployers and other developers must disclose to consumers that they are interacting with an AI system. A rebuttable presumption of reasonable care applies in attorney general enforcement actions where the entity complied with these sections and any rules adopted under section 6-1-1707. Section 4 sets the effective date at 12:01 a.m. the day after the ninety-day period following final adjournment, unless a referendum petition delays it to the November 2026 general election.

Strikeouts and capitals are not visible in plain text, so deleted words appear beside new ones (e.g., 'February 1, 2026 JUNE 30, 2026'; 'promulgated ADOPTED'); this annotation codes the new wording. Registry metadata describes the bill as delaying SB24-205, but the document does not name SB24-205; target_instrument_id is left empty because no registry ID is verifiable from the text. Section 4 gives no calendar date for the effective date. The blank line in 6-1-1702(1) is a formatting artifact.

thresholds.note: SB 25B-004 only changes the effective date of existing provisions in CRS 6-1-1702 to 6-1-1704 from February 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026, and adds no new numeric cutoff for scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation tier, prohibition, benefit, penalty or price. The only other numbers are ninety-day procedural limits (coded as events, not thresholds) and the effective-date clause in Section 4, which is procedural.
